$comment: Every number the gate reports, named once so an idiom's calibration can
refer to it and be wrong in a way somebody notices.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. `patch_behaviour_thresholds.json` says which numbers
a behaviour flag DEMANDS, and every value in it is admitted to be an
untuned guess. An idiom's `listen_for.expect` says which numbers the
technique should PRODUCE, taken from what the technique is meant to sound
like rather than from what a threshold happens to be set to. Those are two
different claims about the same measurement, and having them written in the
same vocabulary is the whole point: where they disagree, one of them is
wrong, and the disagreement is findable (`library_problems` finds it).
A field here has to be one `patch_behaviour.hpp` actually measures, and
every field the thresholds already use has to be here. Both directions are
checked, because either gap turns a calibration into a sentence nothing
`means` is for a reader; `unit` is what the number is in; `higher_is` says
which way the scale runs, because 'expect a low interval_cv' is meaningless
unless you know that low means even.

pitch.voiced_fraction.means: how much of the run had a pitch that could be tracked at all
pitch.voiced_fraction.higher_is: more of the run was pitched

pitch.notes.means: held pitches counted in order, repeats included

pitch.distinct_pitches.means: how many different pitches were played

pitch.pitch_changes.means: how many times the pitch moved

pitch.semitone_range.means: the span from the lowest note to the highest

pitch.median_hz.means: the middle of the pitches played

dynamics.mean_rms.means: the average level across the run

dynamics.end_over_peak.means: how loud the last half second is against the loudest moment

dynamics.duty_cycle.means: how much of the run had sound in it

dynamics.rms_trend.means: whether the level rises or falls across the run

onsets.interval_cv.means: how much the gaps between attacks differ from each other

onsets.interval_trend.means: whether the gaps grow or shrink across the run

onsets.periodicity.means: how strongly the attacks fall on one repeating pulse

onsets.period_ms.means: the pulse the attacks fall on, when there is one

spectrum.centroid_trend.means: whether the sound opens or closes across the run

spectrum.centroid_range_octaves.means: the spread between the darkest and brightest moments

spectrum.active_windows.means: how many analysis windows carried enough signal to have a spectrum
spectrum.active_windows.higher_is: more of the run was measurable
